g.text: A slot represents one ambulance in one dated 12-hour shift.
Selected roster week is within the five-week planning period.
[draft roster exists or no roster exists]
[(1,*) another allocation requested and no invalid-ambulance warning]
SlotSelection is an existing slot ID or a proposed allocation row.
An empty draft offers a proposed row; it becomes a domain slot
only with its chosen ambulance. No new domain attribute is added.
Another allocation iteration returns to shift/slot selection.
No candidate selection or assignment save on this path.
Continue at candidate display for the selected assigned role.
Keep the existing assignment until a replacement is accepted.
[fill a role or replace an existing assignment]
[(1,*) first candidate attempt or previous result is prevented/cancelled]
staff denotes the candidate being evaluated, then the selected staff.
I02: pending-assignment contribution stays in PolicyContext.
I03: dated location is supplied; its data source is unresolved.
A weekly station preference is not treated as dated location.
proposal = selected staff, slot/shift, ambulance, roles and week;
replacedAssignmentId is present only for a replacement.
Exclude that assignment from checks where appropriate,
UC-13 formal baseController binds to roster:RosterController.
No assignment or replacement is saved on this iteration.
Next iteration restarts at candidate retrieval/display.
Exit the candidate loop and proceed to the save step.
[normal save path; assigned ambulance has not been made unavailable]
I07: the source specifies this warning but no continuation
or persistence outcome for the interrupted save step.
This scenario ends at the warning. It cannot enter another
allocation iteration or the successful final draft-save path.
Successful path: stored assignments passed UC-13;
selected ambulances are active, available and have no other
same-shift slot. Draft changes have audit entries.
Staff availability is read/displayed only; it is never modified.
UML 2.5. Boundaries, controllers, value types and operations are proposed detailed design (I08).
Database requests are descriptive; no SQL schema or transaction guarantees are assumed.
Open source details: pending-assignment policy (I02), candidate dated-location source (I03),
and the unavailable-ambulance warning's continuation/persistence outcome (I07).
